themes: Safety, and the product acting on its own

entries.theme: Safety, and the product acting on its own
entries.title: Should the limits watch read Vercel with its own token?
entries.body: Vercel has no read-only token; a token can deploy and delete. Until the app holds one, the new "Plan limits" card is blind to Vercel, the one limit we nearly broke.
entries.recommended: mint a fresh token scoped to the Partyreel team, one-year expiry, as `VERCEL_USAGE_TOKEN` (non-sensitive until launch, then Sensitive). The cron makes one read with it a day. The app's env already holds keys as powerful (the database's service key, R2's write keys).
alternatives: keep Vercel out of the app. A GitHub Action holds the token and posts the numbers in (a workflow and a route to build), or the kit reads it only when an agent runs it

entries.theme: Safety, and the product acting on its own
entries.title: A read-only Cloudflare analytics token for R2's operations and the Workers' requests?
entries.body: `Account Analytics: Read` only: it can't deploy or delete.
entries.recommended: yes, as `CLOUDFLARE_ANALYTICS_TOKEN`; the four meters wait for it.

entries.title: May an open album's "has anything changed?" answer be cached by the CDN for a few seconds?
entries.body: That's the single biggest cost lever: 100 lit phones asking costs one call instead of 100. But a cached answer reaches anyone who has its URL.
entries.recommended: only for an open album at full access, never a password album or a blocked viewer, and the answer is a version number, never photos or links. Not built until you say yes.

entries.title: Should the operator be able to lift a host's uploads count?
entries.body: `/admin/accounts` now shows each host's uploads against her allowance, read-only. A false positive (a bug, a misread meter) would block a paying host with nothing in `/admin` to lift it.
entries.recommended: before launch, an audited credit: a reason, your second factor, a bounded amount, logged in `admin_actions`. Never a reset of the ledger, which the spend watch also reads. It's a migration, so a follow-up lane on your word.

entries.title: A Disposable's develop time when the date comes later.
entries.body: Create now asks the style. With no date yet, a Disposable develops at 9 am tomorrow, and that time never follows a date added later, so a party weeks away would develop before it starts. The row says the time plainly, but it's easy to miss.
entries.recommended: when you set or move the date, an untouched develop time that falls before the party ends moves to the morning after (9 am, your zone). A time you chose yourself never moves.
alternatives: ask the date in Create
put a "morning after" shortcut beside the row

entries.title: Who can act for an event?
entries.body: Today one account owns and runs each event: no co-host, no helper for the night, no hand-over (`events.host_id` is the only owner, assumed by 121 checks in 39 migrations, and the planners post says so in public). Nearly every wedding has two hosts, and Pro's sizes are sold as a planner's year and a venue's year.
entries.recommended: co-hosts invited by email, acting for the event as the owner does (Review, the door, Settings, Share), while billing, storage, the plan and deleting the event stay the owner's; handing an event to another account waits for X14.
alternatives: one owner for good, with a read-only link for a partner
roles per event (owner, co-host, a night helper who runs only Review and the door)
hand-over now

entries.title: What is inside an event, and what does one pass buy?
entries.body: An event is one stream with one reel, one folder and one roll, so a wedding weekend is either one undivided album or several paid events (a competitor sells sub-albums).
entries.recommended: day dividers drawn from the dates and the capture times, display only (no schema, no price change), now; named chapters or linked events only when hosts ask.
alternatives: chapters she names, each with its own reel and folder
a weekend grouping several events under one link and one pass

entries.theme: Safety, and the product acting on its own
entries.title: Who may Partyreel contact, and for what?
entries.body: Account says "Your guests never hear from us" and help promises no "album is ready" mail, yet the ROADMAP plans a guest's develop and let-in mails; and a host hears nothing when her event goes live, when someone waits at her door while she is away, or when the album develops.
entries.recommended: a host's email for her event's moments (a receipt with the code and the print link, a quiet alert for the door and Review while she is away, a morning-after recap); a guest hears from us only when she asks at the door ("Email me when it develops"), once, never marketing: "never" becomes "only when you ask".
alternatives: hosts only, guests never
web push for hosts through an installed app
messages the host writes, sent once

entries.title: Does the album hold words?
entries.body: It holds photographs and videos alone: no caption, no note, no guestbook, though the guestbook is a wedding staple and competitors include one.
entries.recommended: a guestbook as its own kind (a short note, a voice memo or a video message to the hosts), in a room of its own and at the reel's end, moderated in Review like any upload; no captions or comments on photographs, so the album stays the pictures.
alternatives: never, as part of the identity
an optional one-line caption at send
comments and reactions

entries.title: Will a guest ever see Partyreel in her own language?
entries.body: Everything is US English, written inline in about 260 files, and the cost of translating grows with every string.
entries.recommended: English at launch, with the guest's journey (the door, the album, the camera, the reel) made translation-ready now (a string catalog, dates and plurals by her locale); the host's app later.
alternatives: English only for good, said plainly
three to five languages at launch, by the phone's setting
the host picks the album's language

entries.title: Is the professional host (a planner, a venue, a photographer) a launch target?
entries.body: Pro's sizes are sold for them, but nothing exists for them: no hand-over, no partner mark, no templates.
entries.recommended: not at launch: Pro's sizes say what they hold instead, and the professional is decided with X9's hand-over after launch.
alternatives: the minimum now (roles, hand-over, templates)
a partner's mark on the guest page, the prints and the reel as a paid lever
a host theme

entries.title: Will Partyreel ever find a guest's photos by her face?
entries.body: Selfie search is becoming a premium default among competitors, but it is biometric data (Illinois' BIPA, the GDPR's special category).
entries.recommended: never, said as a privacy feature, with ways to find a photograph that need no face (by day, by who sent it, videos, likes).
alternatives: opt-in selfie search per album through a vendor, deleted with the event
tagging yourself
decide later, promising nothing meanwhile

entries.title: Prints or a book?
entries.body: Export is the only way out today; a competitor sells photobooks.
entries.recommended: not before launch; after it, a print partner built on the host's picks.

entries.title: What does a follow do before the feed exists?
entries.body: Nothing reads follows until the after-launch feed (account-moments r2 asks how a follow feels; this asks what it is for).
entries.recommended: keep Follow as a private list (whom she follows, on her page) and say so; its payoff is the feed.
alternatives: hide Follow until the feed ships

entries.title: An Event Pass is one year, paid once.
entries.body: She is reminded before it ends (unless she turned Event Pass reminders off), and a renewal at the cheaper price extends from the end of the year she holds, only while it is still active. When the year ends the account becomes Free: nothing is deleted, but her albums stop taking uploads, hers and her guests', until she renews (AJ1, AR5).
entries.changeIf: a lapsed pass should keep collecting for a grace period, or a renewal should happen by itself.

entries.title: A plan that ends over its storage.
entries.body: She gets 45 days of grace with reminders; at the deadline what she already deleted leaves for good first, then her largest files move to Deleted (30 days to recover) until she is under the cap, with no small overage forgiven.
entries.changeIf: a small overage should be forgiven, or nothing should move without her.

entries.title: Every plan, Free included, can send to Google Drive.
entries.body: It costs us about $0.0003 a GB and is the honest way out; once Free has it, the rule that a marketed number only moves up keeps it there.
entries.changeIf: Drive should be a paid feature: decide before it goes live with milestone 39.

entries.title: A Free event idle for six months is removed.
entries.body: Warned two weeks out, then moved to Deleted (30 days to recover); any use of her account, the event's own dates or a new photo resets the clock; Pro and Event Pass albums never.
entries.changeIf: a Free album should never be removed (events otherwise never expire), or the clock should be longer.

entries.title: The get-ready checklist
entries.body: stays atop an event until it is done or until the day after the event's date; it is only advice, blocks nothing and guests never see it.
entries.changeIf: it should stay until done, whatever the date.

entries.title: When an album turns.
entries.body: After its party an album turns from newest first to the order things happened; the live demo and an album with no date never turn, which is every new album until its host adds a date (Create asks none).
entries.changeIf: an undated album should turn too (her own "In order now", or Create asking a date).

entries.title: How live an open page stays.
entries.body: Where the live line is blocked an album asks for news every 12 seconds, slowing to a minute when quiet; past two untouched hours it stops asking until a touch; a party screen rests at 5 minutes, its doorbell still instant.
entries.changeIf: a long-open page should keep asking (each ask is a call on every open phone).

entries.title: A host's removal spends a guest's shots,
entries.body: as her own take-back does: a guest whose host removed five of her 24 can take only 3 more.
entries.changeIf: a host's removal should give the guest her frames back.

entries.title: Leaving Partyreel
entries.body: keeps her photos in other people's albums unless she ticks "Also remove…".
entries.changeIf: leaving should take her photos by default.

entries.title: A guest's "remove my photo" leaves for good that night
entries.body: on every album, where a host's own delete waits 30 days in Deleted.
entries.changeIf: a guest's removal should wait 30 days too.

entries.title: An open report pauses deletion:
entries.body: a reported album cannot be permanently deleted until the report closes, whatever its date in Deleted, and our evidence copy stays.
entries.changeIf: a host's own deletion should always finish on time.

entries.title: A copy in a host's Google Drive stays hers after a takedown:
entries.body: we delete nothing in her Drive, and our access reaches only the files we made.
entries.changeIf: you want an audited "Delete our copy from her Drive" before launch.

entries.title: No Follow is offered across a block, either way,
entries.body: so a person can infer that someone blocked them, though the page never says which side.
entries.changeIf: Follow should stay offered and fail quietly, keeping every block invisible.

entries.theme: Safety, and the product acting on its own
entries.title: The instant hide
entries.body: (a report that hides a photo at once): one address can hide 3 items a day, one event can lose 5 a day, and a host never triggers it on her own event; when you dismiss the report, the photo comes back (J4).
entries.changeIf: the limits feel off, or a hidden photo should stay down until you look.

entries.theme: Safety, and the product acting on its own
entries.title: Strikes:
entries.body: every dismissed child-abuse report counts against its reporter, even one that hid nothing, and the third dismiss needs no extra confirm.
entries.changeIf: only reports that hid something should count, or the third should ask.

entries.theme: Safety, and the product acting on its own
entries.title: The spend watch
entries.body: checks our usage daily (hourly at launch) and alerts you past ten times the week's busiest day; on its own it pauses only reminders, Download all, Drive and the nightly cleanup until a person lifts it. Uploads only alert (M2: a false alarm must never stop a party), beside your one-press switch that stops guests' uploads.
entries.changeIf: ten times is too loose, a pause should lift itself, or a runaway album should stop itself.
